## Dataset & Libraries
```{r}
# Libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(survey)
library(gtsummary)
library(tableone)
library(here)

#dataset from P3_PartC
nhanes_newvars<- readRDS(here("data", "processed", "nhanes_bmd_pediatric_newvars.rds"))

```


## Examination of Exposure & Evaluation of cell counts
```{r}
# setting male analytic sample
subpop_male <- subset(nhanes_newvars, 
                 subpop1 ==1 & RIAGENDR =="Male")

# setting female analytic sample
subpop_female <- subset(nhanes_newvars, subpop1 ==1 & RIAGENDR =="Female")

# examination of exposure (screen time) and EMM among males 
# frequency table of males
library(dplyr)
library(janitor)
subpop_male %>% 
  mutate(fsdch_2cat = as.character(fsdch_2cat)) %>% 
  tabyl(screen_quart, fsdch_2cat)

# examination of exposure (screen time) and EMM among females
# frequency table of females
subpop_female |> 
  mutate(fsdch_2cat = as.character(fsdch_2cat)) |> 
  tabyl(screen_quart, fsdch_2cat)


# examination of exposure (screen time) and outcome (BMD z-score categorical) 
# among EMM + SEX
## Among food secure males
subpop_male %>% 
    mutate(fsdch_2cat = as.character(fsdch_2cat)) %>% 
  filter(fsdch_2cat == "High/Marginal Food Security") %>% 
  tabyl(screen_quart, bmd_z_cat)

## Among food insecure males
subpop_male %>% 
    mutate(fsdch_2cat = as.character(fsdch_2cat)) %>% 
  filter(fsdch_2cat == "Low/Very Low Food Security") %>% 
  tabyl(screen_quart, bmd_z_cat)

## Among food secure females
subpop_female %>% 
    mutate(fsdch_2cat = as.character(fsdch_2cat)) %>% 
  filter(fsdch_2cat == "High/Marginal Food Security") %>% 
  tabyl(screen_quart, bmd_z_cat)

## Among food insecure females
subpop_female %>% 
    mutate(fsdch_2cat = as.character(fsdch_2cat)) %>% 
  filter(fsdch_2cat == "Low/Very Low Food Security") %>% 
  tabyl(screen_quart, bmd_z_cat)

```
**Cell counts for males and females that are food insecure do not appear to be adequate to produce statistically reliable estimates of proportions.**

## Examination of Outcome from Part C + Graphical Visualization
```{r}
attach(nhanes_newvars)
## Primary survey design
nhanes_design_full <- svydesign(
  id = ~SDMVPSU,
  strata = ~SDMVSTRA,
  weights = ~WTMEC6YR,
  nest = TRUE,
  data = nhanes_newvars)

# Isolating analytic subpop
subpop_design <- subset(nhanes_design_full, subpop1 == 1)

## Prevalence Estimate 
#Estimate prevalence of low BMD (defined as z score less than -2.0) using weighted estimates
svyciprop(~I(bmd_z_cat == "Low TBLH BMD"),
          design=subpop_design,
          method = "logit",
          level = 0.95)

#Estimate prevalence and confidence intervals by sex
gender_prev <- svyby(formula = ~I(bmd_z_cat == "Low TBLH BMD"),
  by = ~RIAGENDR,
  design = subpop_design,
  FUN = svyciprop,
  method = "logit",
  level = 0.95)

confint(gender_prev)

## Mean & Central Tendency 
#Estimate the mean and central tendency of BMD correcting for stratified sampling and survey weights. 
## correcting for stratified sampling and survey weights
svymean(~bmd_zscore_adj, design = subpop_design)


#Estimating the mean and central tendency of BMD by screen time quartiles
svyby(formula = ~bmd_zscore_adj, 
      by = ~factor(screen_quart), 
      design = subpop_design, 
      FUN = svymean, 
      keep.var = TRUE)

#Estimating the mean and central tendency of BMD by screen time quartiles & SEX
svyby(formula = ~bmd_zscore_adj, 
      by = ~factor(screen_quart), 
      design = subset(subpop_design, RIAGENDR =="Male"), # by sex male
      FUN = svymean, 
      keep.var = TRUE)

svyby(formula = ~bmd_zscore_adj, 
      by = ~factor(screen_quart), 
      design = subset(subpop_design, RIAGENDR =="Female"), # by sex female
      FUN = svymean, 
      keep.var = TRUE)

# weighted histogram of BMD adjusted z-score
## weighted histogram of analytic sample
svyhist(~bmd_zscore_adj, 
        design = subpop_design, 
        breaks = 30)

# weighted histogram by male sex
svyhist(~bmd_zscore_adj, 
        design = subset(subpop_design, RIAGENDR =="Male"), 
        breaks = 30)

# weighted histogram by female sex
svyhist(~bmd_zscore_adj, 
        design = subset(subpop_design, RIAGENDR =="Female"), 
        breaks = 30)


# weighted boxplot of BMD adjusted z-score
## weighted boxplot
svyboxplot(bmd_zscore_adj~1, 
           design = subpop_design)

# weighted boxplot by male sex
svyboxplot(bmd_zscore_adj~1, 
           design = subset(subpop_design, RIAGENDR =="Male"))

# weighted boxplot by female sex
svyboxplot(bmd_zscore_adj~1, 
           design = subset(subpop_design, RIAGENDR =="Female"))
```

## Visualization of Exposure and Outcome with Linearity & Normality Evaluation
```{r}
## Visualization of Linearity in Exposure and Outcome ##
# Among male subpop
ggplot(subpop_male, 
       aes(x = as.numeric(screen_quart), y = bmd_zscore_adj)) +
  geom_jitter(size = 1, alpha = .6, width = 0.2) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", size = 8, shape = 18) +
  geom_smooth(method = lm, se = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "Screen time Quartiles", 
       y = "BMD adjusted z-scores",
       title = "BMD z-scores vs. screen time quartiles among 8-17 y.o males",
       caption = "Diamonds = screen time level averages") +
  theme(axis.title = element_text(size = 10), 
        axis.text = element_text(size = 10), 
        title = element_text(size = 10), 
        axis.text.x=element_text(angle = 10, vjust = 1, hjust=1))

# Among female subpop
ggplot(subpop_female, 
       aes(x = as.numeric(screen_quart), y = bmd_zscore_adj)) +
  geom_jitter(size = 1, alpha = .6, width = 0.2) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", size = 8, shape = 18) +
  geom_smooth(method = lm, se = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "Screen time Quartiles", 
       y = "BMD adjusted z-scores",
       title = "BMD z-scores vs. screen time quartiles among 8-17 y.o females",
       caption = "Diamonds = screen time level averages") +
  theme(axis.title = element_text(size = 10), 
        axis.text = element_text(size = 10), 
        title = element_text(size = 10), 
        axis.text.x=element_text(angle = 10, vjust = 1, hjust=1))

## Normality##
##Evaluation of distribution of outcome with QQ plot among male subpop
# linear regression
model_male <- svyglm(bmd_zscore_adj~screen_quart, 
                     design = subset(subpop_design, RIAGENDR =="Male"))

#augment to extract residuals (.resid)
aug_male <- augment(model_male)
glimpse(aug_male)

#creating QQ plot
ggplot(aug_male, 
       aes(sample = .resid)) + 
  stat_qq() + 
  stat_qq_line()

##Evaluation of distribution of outcome with QQ plot among female subpop
# linear regression
model_female <- svyglm(bmd_zscore_adj~screen_quart, 
                     design = subset(subpop_design, RIAGENDR =="Female"))

#augment to extract residuals (.resid)
aug_female <- augment(model_female)
glimpse(aug_female)

#creating QQ plot
ggplot(aug_female, 
       aes(sample = .resid)) + 
  stat_qq() + 
  stat_qq_line()

```
## Visualization of Linearity of other Continuous Independent Variables
```{r}
## Age as a Continuous Variable ##
# creating a scatterplot in male subpop
nhanes_newvars%>% 
  filter(subpop1==1 & RIAGENDR =="Male")  %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = RIDAGEYR, 
             y = bmd_zscore_adj)) + 
  geom_point(position = position_jitter(width = 0.3, height = 0.1)) + 
  labs(title = "Scatterplot of Age and BMD z-score", 
      y = "BMD z-score")

# overlaying a LOESS (locally weighted regression) plot
nhanes_newvars%>% 
  filter(subpop1==1 & RIAGENDR =="Male")  %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = bmd_zscore_adj, 
             y = RIDAGEYR)) +
  geom_point() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", 
              span = 0.75, 
              se = F, 
              color = "green") +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", 
              span = 0.25, 
              se = F, 
              color = "red", 
              linetype = 2) + 
  theme_classic() 

# Fit the crude model with the linear age term and output the linear predictor
## Using survey specifications coded above with same analytic sample
## run the model among males
crude_age_model <- svyglm(bmd_zscore_adj~RIDAGEYR, 
                     design = subset(subpop_design, RIAGENDR =="Male"))

summary(crude_age_model)

# Get fitted values
aug_age <- augment(crude_age_model)

# plot the model-predicted linear outcome versus age
ggplot(data = aug_age, 
       aes(x = RIDAGEYR, 
           y = .fitted)) + 
  geom_smooth() + 
  labs(x = "Age at Screening", 
       y = "Value of the Linear Predictor") + 
  theme_classic()

## Higher order predictors
# find mean in subpop
svymean(~RIDAGEYR, design = subpop_design) # weighted mean = 12.482

# create centered variables
nhanes_newvars <- nhanes_newvars %>% 
  mutate(agec = RIDAGEYR - 12.482, 
         agec_sq = agec^2, 
         agec_cu = agec^3)

## Quadratic model
## re-run survey specifications
nhanes_design_quad <- svydesign(
  id = ~SDMVPSU,
  strata = ~SDMVSTRA,
  weights = ~WTMEC6YR,
  nest = TRUE,
  data = nhanes_newvars)

# setting analytic sample
subpop_quad <- subset(nhanes_design_quad, 
                 subpop1 ==1)

## run the model
crude_model_quad <- svyglm(bmd_zscore_adj~agec+agec_sq, 
                      design = subset(subpop_quad, RIAGENDR =="Male"))

summary(crude_model_quad)

# Get fitted values
model_aug_quad <- augment(crude_model_quad)

ggplot(data = model_aug_quad, 
       aes(x = agec + 12.482, 
           y = .fitted)) + 
  geom_smooth() + 
  labs(x = "Age at Screening", 
       y = "Value of the Linear Predictor", 
       title = "Quadratic Model") + 
  theme_classic()

## Cubic Model
## run the model
crude_model_cube <- svyglm(bmd_zscore_adj~agec+agec_sq+agec_cu, 
                       design = subset(subpop_quad, RIAGENDR =="Male"))

summary(crude_model_cube)

# Get fitted values
model_aug_cube <- augment(crude_model_cube)

ggplot(data = model_aug_cube, 
       aes(x = agec + 12.482, 
           y = .fitted)) + 
  geom_smooth() + 
  labs(x = "Age at Screening", 
       y = "Value of the Linear Predictor", 
       title = "Cubic Model") + 
  theme_classic()

library(describedata)
gladder(subpop_male$RIDAGEYR) # looking to see if age should be transformed 
# to another power not evaluated. Hard to tell 


###### Poverty Income Ratio (PIR) as a Continuous Variable #####
# creating a scatterplot in male subpop
nhanes_newvars%>% 
  filter(subpop1==1 & RIAGENDR =="Male")  %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = INDFMPIR, 
             y = bmd_zscore_adj)) + 
  geom_point(position = position_jitter(width = 0.3, height = 0.1)) + 
  labs(title = "Scatterplot of PIR and BMD z-score", 
      y = "BMD z-score")

# overlaying a LOESS (locally weighted regression) plot
nhanes_newvars%>% 
  filter(subpop1==1 & RIAGENDR =="Male")  %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = bmd_zscore_adj, 
             y = INDFMPIR)) +
  geom_point() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", 
              span = 0.75, 
              se = F, 
              color = "green") +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", 
              span = 0.25, 
              se = F, 
              color = "red", 
              linetype = 2) + 
  theme_classic() 

# Fit the crude model with the linear age term and output the linear predictor
## Using survey specifications coded above with same analytic sample
## run the model among males
crude_pir_model <- svyglm(bmd_zscore_adj~INDFMPIR, 
                     design = subset(subpop_design, RIAGENDR =="Male"))

summary(crude_pir_model)

# Get fitted values
aug_pir <- augment(crude_pir_model)

# plot the model-predicted linear outcome versus age
ggplot(data = aug_pir, 
       aes(x = INDFMPIR, 
           y = .fitted)) + 
  geom_smooth() + 
  labs(x = "Poverty Income Ratio at Screening", 
       y = "Value of the Linear Predictor") + 
  theme_classic()

## Create higher order predictors
nhanes_newvars <- nhanes_newvars %>% 
  mutate(pir = INDFMPIR, 
         pir_sq = pir^2, 
         pir_cu = pir^3)

## Quadratic model
## re-run survey specifications
nhanes_design_quad_pir <- svydesign(
  id = ~SDMVPSU,
  strata = ~SDMVSTRA,
  weights = ~WTMEC6YR,
  nest = TRUE,
  data = nhanes_newvars)

# setting analytic sample
subpop_quad_pir <- subset(nhanes_design_quad_pir, 
                 subpop1 ==1)

## run the model
crude_model_quad_pir <- svyglm(bmd_zscore_adj~pir+pir_sq, 
                      design = subset(subpop_quad_pir, RIAGENDR =="Male"))

summary(crude_model_quad_pir)

# Get fitted values
model_aug_quad_pir <- augment(crude_model_quad_pir)

ggplot(data = model_aug_quad_pir, 
       aes(x = pir, 
           y = .fitted)) + 
  geom_smooth() + 
  labs(x = "Poverty Income ratio at Screening", 
       y = "Value of the Linear Predictor", 
       title = "Quadratic Model") + 
  theme_classic()

## Cubic Model
## run the model
crude_model_cube_pir <- svyglm(bmd_zscore_adj~pir+pir_sq+pir_cu, 
                       design = subset(subpop_quad_pir, RIAGENDR =="Male"))

summary(crude_model_cube_pir)

# Get fitted values
model_aug_cube_pir <- augment(crude_model_cube_pir)

ggplot(data = model_aug_cube_pir, 
       aes(x = pir, 
           y = .fitted)) + 
  geom_smooth() + 
  labs(x = "Poverty Income Ratio at Screening", 
       y = "Value of the Linear Predictor", 
       title = "Cubic Model") + 
  theme_classic()


pir_clean <- subpop_male %>% 
  filter(INDFMPIR > 0 & !is.na(INDFMPIR)) %>% 
  pull(INDFMPIR)

gladder(pir_clean) # looking to see if PIR should be transformed 
# to another power not evaluated. The best one appears to be "identity". 

```
